Scaffolding goes up on Monday

Works begin at the north face

NAIROBI — Contractors arrive at first light on Monday to begin work on the cathedral's north face, the diocese said in a statement released on Friday. The project has been in planning for more than a decade, delayed by funding shortfalls and two changes of architect, and is expected to take eighteen months to complete.

What is happening

The first phase covers the lower courses of masonry, where water ingress has done the most damage. Engineers will remove and catalogue each stone before it is cleaned, repaired or replaced with freshly quarried limestone from the same seam that supplied the original builders in the fourteenth century.

  • Stone survey and cataloguing
  • Cleaning and consolidation
    • Lime mortar repointing
  • Replacement of failed blocks

Deliveries come by the west gate. The diocese has promised a hotline for complaints and a monthly open evening at which the engineers will show what they have found, a practice borrowed from a similar programme at another cathedral that reported far fewer objections once people could see the stones for themselves.

A final paragraph rounds off the piece with enough words to keep the readability score comfortable, noting that the works order was signed on Thursday and that the first stones will come down before the end of the month, weather permitting, according to the clerk of works who has overseen three such projects before this one.
